newsitem.title: CHILE: Banco Santiago sees $150 mln capital boost.
newsitem.headline: Banco Santiago sees $150 mln capital boost.

text.p: Banco Santiago plans a $150 million capital increase to allow it to meet the so-called Basle requirements for financial institutions as set by Chile's proposed General Banking Law, the bank said in a statement.

The capital increase, proposed by the board of directors, will be through shares offered to shareholders who will also be entitled to acquire those shares not purchased by other shareholders. The price of each share will be eight Chilean pesos, payable in cash, said the statement.

The statement left out many key details of the proposed capital increase, such as the total amount of the rise, when the bank will place the shares, and whether it will place them on both foreign and local markets.
The bank also said it will offer for sale 35.1 billion Banco Santiago E series shares, representing 38.527 percent of equity capital, on behalf of the Central Bank.

The Central Bank currently holds the shares as payment from Banco Santiago for debts incurred during Chile's banking crisis in the early 1980s. Banco Santiago turned the shares over to the Central Bank last year when the private institution was created in the merger of Banco O'Higgins and Banco de Santiago.
The shares will be offered at 12.82 Chilean pesos a share, said the statement, considerably higher than the shares to be sold through the capital increase.

Referring to the E series, the statement said "this offer is extended to the shareholders of record on April 28, 1997, of any series of Banco Santiago stock. Each shareholder will be entitled to purchase 0.6267309 shares..." Shareholders will have until June 4, 1997, to accept the offer, the statement said.

The General Banking Law, proposed by President Eduardo Frei's government and currently in Congress, would liberalize Chilean banking regulations and bring them more in line with international standards in various aspects of the banking business, officials say.
